extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to the Fulbright U.S. Student Program (U.S. citizens — current students, recent graduates/non-enrolled applicants, and artists; also informational for non-U.S. citizens seeking Fulbright to the U.S.)
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step official guidance for determining eligibility, choosing the correct award type, and completing/submitting an application to the Fulbright U.S. Student Program (through a campus Fulbright Program Adviser or as an At-Large applicant). Includes deadlines, campus review process, and award-specific guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Current U.S. Student
rubrics_metrics.description: United States citizens who are currently enrolled in undergraduate or graduate degree programs are eligible to apply. If you are currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program at a U.S. college or university, you will apply through that institution, even if you are not currently a resident there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find the Fulbright Program Adviser (FPA) on your campus. Applicants enrolled at a U.S. institution are strongly encouraged to apply through that institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — U.S. Citizen but not a Student
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a U.S. citizen, will hold a bachelor’s degree by the award start date, and do not have a Ph.D. degree, then you are eligible to apply. Non-enrolled applicants should have relatively limited professional experience in the fields (typically 7 years or less) in which they are applying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates with more experience should consider applying for the Fulbright Scholar Program. Non-enrolled applicants may apply through their most recent U.S.-based institution that has an FPA if that institution will accommodate alumni applications; otherwise they apply At-Large.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Artists / Creative & Performing Arts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fulbright U.S. Student Program welcomes applications in the creative and performing arts. Arts candidates for the U.S. Student Program should have relatively limited professional experience in the fields (typically 7 years or less).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists with more experience should consider the Fulbright Scholar Program. Creative & Performing Arts projects fall under the Study/Research grant category and are available in all countries where Study/Research grants are offered. Arts applicants should proceed to the Creative & Performing Arts Fields of Study section for information about available fields and supplementary materials requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — U.S. Professors/Administrators (FPA/Scholars Pathway)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a U.S. citizen and a professor or administrator at a U.S. institution and are interested in applying for a Fulbright Scholar Award, you will need to apply through fulbrightscholars.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To support student applicants, connect with the Fulbright Program Adviser at your institution and consult FPA resources, trainings, and webinars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Non U.S. Citizens (applying to U.S.)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a non-U.S. citizen interested in applying for a Fulbright Award to the United States, you will need to apply through the Fulbright Commission or U.S. Embassy in your home country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See information on the Fulbright Visiting Scholar Program or Fulbright Foreign Student Program for country-specific procedures and eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Pathway — Institutional vs At-Large
rubrics_metrics.description: You will apply either through a U.S. institution or At-Large. If you are currently enrolled in a U.S. college or university, you are strongly encouraged to apply through that institution. If not enrolled, you may apply through your most recent U.S.-based institution that has an FPA (if the institution will accommodate alumni applications); all other candidates will apply as At-Large applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide early which pathway applies to you and confirm with an FPA whether alumni applications are accepted if you intend to use a former institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Campus Application Procedure (for applicants applying through U.S. institutions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fulbright Program Adviser (FPA) will set a campus application deadline for the institution’s students, which is typically 4–6 weeks earlier than the final October deadline. All candidates applying through a U.S. institution must complete the Fulbright application through the online system by the campus deadline; all supporting materials as outlined in the Application Components section must also be included by the campus deadline date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You will mark your application 'Ready for Campus Review' once it is complete and it will lock your application for the duration of the campus review. The FPA will schedule a campus interview. Following the interview and before the national deadline you may have the opportunity to revise your application based on feedback; the FPA will unlock your application after campus review is complete. You are responsible for submitting your own application before the National Deadline; your FPA cannot submit on your behalf. Application submissions are final.

rubrics_metrics.name: At‑Large Application Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: At-Large candidates must submit their applications through the Fulbright online application system by the national deadline. Candidates are responsible for ensuring that all supporting documents are attached to the online application, as outlined in the Application Components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application submissions are final. Applications cannot be unsubmitted for any reason. Carefully review application proof for accuracy prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Submission Finality and Applicant Responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Application submissions are final. Applications cannot be unsubmitted for any reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are responsible for submitting your own application before the National Deadline; your Fulbright Program Adviser cannot do this on your behalf. Carefully review your application and supporting materials before final submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and Timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The national deadline is Tuesday October 6, 2026 at 5 pm Eastern Time. The application is open annually from early April to mid-October; applicants applying through an institution will prepare a completed application by their campus deadlines prior to the national deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm your campus deadline with your FPA (typically 4–6 weeks earlier than the national deadline) and check the Competition Timeline for cycle dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting Materials Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All supporting materials as outlined in the Application Components section must be included with the application (by campus deadline for institutional applicants; attached to the online application for At-Large applicants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Application Components pages (Study/Research: Academic; Study/Research: Creative & Performing Arts; ETA; etc.) for field-specific required documents and any supplementary materials. Use the Application Components guidance to ensure completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award Type — Study/Research Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Study/Research awards are offered for projects in all Academic and Creative & Performing Arts fields. Applicants can propose their own independent study/research projects, or, in some countries, can propose to enroll in a graduate program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arts applicants should consult the Creative & Performing Arts Fields of Study section for available fields and supplementary materials requirements. Use Tutorial Videos and Webinars and Award Search to help determine fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award Type — English Teaching Assistant (ETA) Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: ETA awards place grantees in educational centers overseas to supplement local English language instruction and to provide a fluent speaker presence in the classrooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceed to the English Teaching Assistant Award section to see the countries offering this grant and specific requirements for ETA placements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award Type — Fulbright‑Fogarty Fellowships in Public Health
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fulbright-Fogarty Fellowships in Public Health are offered in partnership with the Fogarty International Center (NIH) and are designed for candidates currently enrolled in medical school or in a graduate-level program who are interested in global health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The basic requirements and application process for Fulbright-Fogarty are the same as for any Fulbright U.S. Student Study/Research Grant; consult the Fulbright-Fogarty section for program-specific details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources for Choosing Award and Preparing Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Tutorial Videos and Webinars can assist you in learning more about each award type. Award Search allows you to narrow down opportunities by educational background, grant type, and world area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these resources early to identify appropriate awards, country-specific opportunities, and required application components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Country Opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Select country(ies) of interest and review available awards and eligibility requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Country-specific awards and eligibility can vary — review each country/post listing and the Award Search tool to confirm availability and any additional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Application Components
rubrics_metrics.description: Before starting an application, review the Application Components section(s) relevant to your award type (Study/Research: Academic, Creative & Performing Arts, ETA, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application Components pages contain the detailed list of required documents, supplementary materials, and instructions needed for a complete submission.
